## How to read this file

The HSSC technical check (Submission ID dec96048-eb1b-4977-a973-b7bc7dd040f7)
asked us to report the results accurately. Revising the manuscript added or
corrected a set of numbers. This notebook recomputes **each of those numbers
from the raw data files in `Results/`** and compares it with the value printed
in the final manuscript.

Each section follows the same layout:

1. **Claim**: the sentence as printed, and where it appears (final PDF line
   numbers).
2. **Computation**: the code, folded. Click *Code* to open it.
3. **Check**: the reported value, the recomputed value, and whether they agree
   after rounding to the number of digits printed in the manuscript.

The last section collects every check in one table. All checks should show
✅. The table is also saved as `outputs/check_summary.csv`.

This notebook only adds checks. It does not change or replace the original
analysis pipeline in `Analysis_script/` (`02_statistical_analysis.R` and the
other scripts), which produced the submitted results.

**To render**, open this file in RStudio and click **Render**, or run this
from the repository root:

```bash
quarto render Minor_revision_technical_check/recomputed_values.qmd
```

Required R packages: `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `lme4`, `knitr`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup: packages, paths and helper functions"
needed <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "lme4", "knitr")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Install these R packages first: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(lme4)
})
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

# Find the repository root (the folder that contains Results/).
find_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  d <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(d, "Results", "SDO_VSA_Results_20260830.csv"))) return(d)
    up <- dirname(d)
    if (identical(up, d)) stop("Cannot find the Results folder.")
    d <- up
  }
}
root    <- find_root()
out_dir <- file.path(root, "Minor_revision_technical_check", "outputs")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

SEED   <- 20260922   # same seed as 02_statistical_analysis.R
B_BOOT <- 20000      # 10 × the original 2,000 resamples, so the limits are stable (see Section 3.3)

# ---- check register --------------------------------------------------------
# Each check stores the value as printed and the recomputed value.
# `digits` = decimals printed in the manuscript; `sig` = significant figures
# for P values printed as a × 10^k.
checks <- tibble()
check <- function(section, location, quantity, reported, value,
                  digits = NULL, sig = NULL, pct = FALSE) {
  shown <- if (!is.null(sig)) {
    formatC(signif(value, sig), format = "e", digits = sig - 1)
  } else if (pct) {
    sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), value)
  } else {
    formatC(round(value, digits), format = "f", digits = digits)
  }
  rep_num <- if (!is.null(sig)) {
    formatC(as.numeric(reported), format = "e", digits = sig - 1)
  } else if (pct) {
    sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), as.numeric(reported))
  } else {
    formatC(as.numeric(reported), format = "f", digits = digits)
  }
  row <- tibble(section = section, location = location, quantity = quantity,
                reported = rep_num, recomputed = shown,
                unrounded = signif(value, 6),
                agrees = ifelse(rep_num == shown, "✅", "❌"))
  checks <<- bind_rows(checks, row)
  invisible(row)
}
show_checks <- function(sec) {
  checks |> filter(section == sec) |>
    select(Location = location, Quantity = quantity, Reported = reported,
           Recomputed = recomputed, Agrees = agrees) |>
    knitr::kable(align = "llrrc")
}

# Developer from the endpoint name.
developer_of <- function(m) {
  m <- tolower(m)
  case_when(grepl("gpt", m) ~ "OpenAI", grepl("claude", m) ~ "Anthropic",
            grepl("gemma", m) ~ "Google", grepl("llama", m) ~ "Meta",
            grepl("qwen", m) ~ "Alibaba", TRUE ~ NA_character_)
}

# Exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test that allows tied |differences|.
# (R's wilcox.test() cannot give an exact P value with ties and switches to a
# normal approximation.) Ranks are doubled so midranks become integers, and
# the null distribution of the signed-rank sum is built by convolution.
exact_signed_rank <- function(d) {
  d  <- d[d != 0]
  r  <- rank(abs(d))
  r2 <- as.integer(round(2 * r))
  V  <- sum(r[d > 0])
  tot  <- sum(r2)
  dist <- c(1, numeric(tot))
  for (k in r2) {
    shifted <- c(numeric(k), dist[seq_len(tot + 1 - k)])
    dist <- dist + shifted
  }
  dist <- dist / sum(dist)
  s   <- 0:tot                        # possible values of 2V
  obs <- abs(round(2 * V) - tot / 2)  # distance of the observed 2V from its null mean
  p   <- sum(dist[abs(s - tot / 2) >= obs - 1e-9])
  list(V = V, p = min(1, p), n = length(d))
}

# Pigeonhole bootstrap (Owen, 2007): resample models and items independently.
# Identical to crossed_boot() in 02_statistical_analysis.R.
crossed_boot <- function(P, B = B_BOOT) {
  nr <- nrow(P); nc <- ncol(P)
  bs <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    mean(P[sample.int(nr, nr, TRUE), sample.int(nc, nc, TRUE), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
  c(estimate = mean(P, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower = unname(quantile(bs, .025)), upper = unname(quantile(bs, .975)))
}
```

## Data and exclusions

**Claim** (Methods 2.3, lines 264–265): the 6,210 attitude calls and the 7,560
RMET calls exclude the failed calls to the excluded endpoint (Claude Sonnet 4).

The rule matches the original script: an endpoint is excluded if more than 50%
of its calls were API errors. A non-numeric answer from a retained model counts
as missing.

```{r}
#| label: data
#| code-summary: "Read the raw files and apply the exclusion rule"
att_raw  <- read_csv(file.path(root, "Results", "SDO_VSA_Results_20260830.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
rmet_raw <- read_csv(file.path(root, "Results", "RMET_Results_20260912.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

api_share <- function(df) df |>
  group_by(model_label) |>
  summarise(calls = n(), api_errors = sum(parse_error %in% "API_ERROR")) |>
  mutate(share = api_errors / calls, excluded = share > .5)
att_audit  <- api_share(att_raw)
rmet_audit <- api_share(rmet_raw)
excluded <- union(att_audit$model_label[att_audit$excluded],
                  rmet_audit$model_label[rmet_audit$excluded])

att  <- att_raw  |> filter(!model_label %in% excluded) |>
  mutate(run = as.integer(.data[["repeat"]]) + 1L, developer = developer_of(model_label))
rmet <- rmet_raw |> filter(!model_label %in% excluded) |>
  mutate(run = as.integer(.data[["repeat"]]) + 1L)

bind_rows(
  att_audit  |> filter(api_errors > 0) |> mutate(file = "Attitudes"),
  rmet_audit |> filter(api_errors > 0) |> mutate(file = "RMET")) |>
  select(file, model_label, calls, api_errors, share, excluded) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Endpoints with any API errors")

sec <- "Data"
check(sec, "Methods 2.3, l. 264", "Attitude calls after exclusion", 6210, nrow(att), digits = 0)
check(sec, "Methods 2.3, l. 264", "RMET calls after exclusion", 7560, nrow(rmet), digits = 0)
check(sec, "Methods 2.3", "Attitude models", 27, n_distinct(att$model_label), digits = 0)
check(sec, "Methods 2.3", "RMET models", 21, n_distinct(rmet$model_label), digits = 0)
show_checks(sec)
```

Excluded endpoint: **`r paste(excluded, collapse = ", ")`**.

## Section 3.2: English versus Chinese SDO6

**Claim** (lines 382–385): "Chinese SDO6 scores exceeded English scores for 26
of 27 models (pooled means 1.79 versus 1.48; SDs across models 0.48 and 0.32;
mean difference 0.31, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.42; paired t-test across models,
t(26) = 6.21, P = 1.5 × 10⁻⁶, d<sub>z</sub> = 1.19; Wilcoxon signed-rank test,
V = 373, P = 1.5 × 10⁻⁷)".

Items 9–16 are reverse-keyed as `8 − value`, so 1 is most egalitarian. Each
model's score is the mean of its numeric answers in each language. The test
compares the 27 Chinese-minus-English differences with zero. d<sub>z</sub> is
the mean difference divided by the SD of the differences.

```{r}
#| label: sdo6
#| code-summary: "Model-level scores and paired tests"
sdo6 <- att |>
  filter(instrument == "SDO6") |>
  mutate(item_no = as.integer(item_no),
         score = if_else(item_no >= 9L, 8 - value, value))

language_test <- function(drop_items = integer(0)) {
  d <- sdo6 |> filter(!item_no %in% drop_items, !is.na(score))
  mm <- d |> group_by(model_label, developer, language) |>
    summarise(m = mean(score)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = language, values_from = m) |>
    mutate(diff = zh - en) |> ungroup()
  tt <- t.test(mm$zh, mm$en, paired = TRUE)
  w  <- exact_signed_rank(mm$diff)
  list(mm = mm, data = d,
       pooled_en = mean(d$score[d$language == "en"]),
       pooled_zh = mean(d$score[d$language == "zh"]),
       sd_en = sd(mm$en), sd_zh = sd(mm$zh),
       diff = mean(mm$diff), ci = unname(tt$conf.int),
       t = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter), p = tt$p.value,
       dz = mean(mm$diff) / sd(mm$diff), V = w$V, p_w = w$p,
       higher = sum(mm$diff > 0), n = nrow(mm))
}
L_all <- language_test()

with(L_all, tibble(
  `Pooled mean, Chinese` = pooled_zh, `Pooled mean, English` = pooled_en,
  `SD across models, Chinese` = sd_zh, `SD across models, English` = sd_en,
  `Mean difference` = diff, `95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", ci[1], ci[2]),
  t = t, df = df, P = format.pval(p, digits = 3), dz = dz, V = V,
  `P (Wilcoxon)` = format.pval(p_w, digits = 3), `Models higher in Chinese` = higher)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), values_transform = as.character) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Statistic", "Value"))

sec <- "3.2 Language"
loc <- "Results 3.2, l. 382–385"
with(L_all, {
  check(sec, loc, "Models higher in Chinese (of 27)", 26, higher, digits = 0)
  check(sec, loc, "Pooled mean, Chinese", 1.79, pooled_zh, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "Pooled mean, English", 1.48, pooled_en, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "SD across models, Chinese", 0.48, sd_zh, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "SD across models, English", 0.32, sd_en, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "Mean difference", 0.31, diff, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "95% CI, lower", 0.21, ci[1], digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "95% CI, upper", 0.42, ci[2], digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "t(26)", 6.21, t, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "P, paired t test", 1.5e-6, p, sig = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "dz", 1.19, dz, digits = 2)
  check(sec, loc, "Wilcoxon V", 373, V, digits = 0)
  check(sec, loc, "P, Wilcoxon (exact)", 1.5e-7, p_w, sig = 2)
})
show_checks(sec)
```

R's built-in `wilcox.test()` gives the same V. Because some |differences| are
tied, it cannot give an exact P value and switches to a normal approximation
(P = `r signif(suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(L_all$mm$zh, L_all$mm$en, paired = TRUE))$p.value, 2)`).
The exact P value above handles the ties directly.

**Correction for the Supplementary Information.** The round-2 draft of the SI
Notes and Table S4 gave P = 5.5 × 10⁻⁶ for the Wilcoxon test without items 2,
4 and 8. That value came from a routine that ignores tied ranks. The exact value
that allows for ties is **5.3 × 10⁻⁶** (next section). For all 16 items both
methods give 1.5 × 10⁻⁷, so the main text is unaffected.

## Section 3.2: robustness checks

**Claim** (lines 409–413): "The difference also persisted without the three
items with non-standard Chinese wording (items 2, 4 and 8; mean difference
0.25, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.35; 23 of 27 models higher in Chinese). Allowing for
developer in a mixed model gave a similar but less precise estimate (0.37,
95% CI 0.05 to 0.70), because only five developers were represented."

The full results go in the Supplementary Notes ("Language analyses") and
Table S4.

### Without the items with non-standard Chinese wording


### Allowing for developer

Most models (21 of 27) came from OpenAI or Anthropic, so models from the same
developer may not be independent. The model-level mixed model regresses each
model's Chinese-minus-English difference on an intercept, with a random
intercept for developer (REML). With only five developers, the main CI uses a
t distribution with 4 degrees of freedom (number of developers − 1). The
normal-theory (Wald) interval is also shown. The response-level model uses
every answer: item as a fixed effect, and random intercepts and language slopes
for developer and for model.

```{r}
#| label: robust-developer
#| code-summary: "Mixed models with developer as a random effect"
mixed_model_level <- function(x) {
  fit <- lmer(diff ~ 1 + (1 | developer), data = x$mm, REML = TRUE)
  est <- fixef(fit)[[1]]; se <- sqrt(vcov(fit)[1, 1]); k <- n_distinct(x$mm$developer)
  tibble(estimate = est, se = se,
         ci_t_lo = est - qt(.975, k - 1) * se, ci_t_hi = est + qt(.975, k - 1) * se,
         p_t = 2 * pt(-abs(est / se), k - 1),
         ci_wald_lo = est - qnorm(.975) * se, ci_wald_hi = est + qnorm(.975) * se,
         p_wald = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)))
}
M_all <- mixed_model_level(L_all)
M_248 <- mixed_model_level(L_248)

resp <- L_all$data |> mutate(zh = as.integer(language == "zh"), item = factor(item_no))
fit_resp <- lmer(score ~ zh + item + (1 + zh | developer) + (1 | model_label) + (0 + zh | model_label),
                 data = resp, REML = TRUE)
est_r <- fixef(fit_resp)[["zh"]]; se_r <- sqrt(vcov(fit_resp)["zh", "zh"])
M_resp <- tibble(estimate = est_r, se = se_r,
                 ci_t_lo = est_r - qt(.975, 4) * se_r, ci_t_hi = est_r + qt(.975, 4) * se_r,
                 p_t = 2 * pt(-abs(est_r / se_r), 4))

bind_rows(M_all |> mutate(Model = "Model level, all items"),
          M_248 |> mutate(Model = "Model level, without 2, 4, 8"),
          M_resp |> mutate(Model = "Response level, all items")) |>
  relocate(Model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "ci_t / p_t use t with 4 df; ci_wald / p_wald use the normal distribution")

dev_means <- L_all$mm |> group_by(developer) |>
  summarise(models = n(), mean_difference = mean(diff)) |> arrange(developer)
knitr::kable(dev_means, digits = 3, caption = "Mean Chinese-minus-English difference by developer")

sec <- "3.2 Robustness"
check(sec, "Results 3.2, l. 411–413", "Developer-adjusted estimate", 0.37, M_all$estimate, digits = 2)
check(sec, "Results 3.2, l. 411–413", "Developer-adjusted 95% CI lower (t, 4 df)", 0.05, M_all$ci_t_lo, digits = 2)
check(sec, "Results 3.2, l. 411–413", "Developer-adjusted 95% CI upper (t, 4 df)", 0.70, M_all$ci_t_hi, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Developer-adjusted SE", 0.12, M_all$se, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes / Table S4", "Developer-adjusted P (t, 4 df)", 0.033, M_all$p_t, digits = 3)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Developer-adjusted Wald CI lower", 0.14, M_all$ci_wald_lo, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Developer-adjusted Wald CI upper", 0.60, M_all$ci_wald_hi, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Response-level estimate", 0.37, M_resp$estimate, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Response-level 95% CI lower (t, 4 df)", 0.04, M_resp$ci_t_lo, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Response-level 95% CI upper (t, 4 df)", 0.69, M_resp$ci_t_hi, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes / Table S4", "Without 2, 4, 8: developer-adjusted estimate", 0.28, M_248$estimate, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes / Table S4", "Without 2, 4, 8: 95% CI lower (t, 4 df)", -0.03, M_248$ci_t_lo, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes / Table S4", "Without 2, 4, 8: 95% CI upper (t, 4 df)", 0.58, M_248$ci_t_hi, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes / Table S4", "Without 2, 4, 8: P (t, 4 df)", 0.064, M_248$p_t, digits = 3)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Without 2, 4, 8: Wald CI lower", 0.06, M_248$ci_wald_lo, digits = 2)
check(sec, "SI Notes", "Without 2, 4, 8: Wald CI upper", 0.49, M_248$ci_wald_hi, digits = 2)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(dev_means))) {
  rep_val <- c(Alibaba = 0.15, Anthropic = 0.26, Google = 0.45, Meta = 0.80, OpenAI = 0.24)[[dev_means$developer[i]]]
  check(sec, "SI Notes", paste("Developer mean difference,", dev_means$developer[i]),
        rep_val, dev_means$mean_difference[i], digits = 2)
}
show_checks(sec)
```

## Section 3.1: RMET accuracy and spread

**Claim** (lines 362–364): "the models chose the consensus ('correct') word on
74% of items (26.7 of 36, SD 3.7 across models), close to the adult average of
26.2 (SD 3.6; Baron-Cohen et al., 2001; difference 0.5 items, 95% CI −1.3 to
2.3)."

Each model's accuracy is averaged over runs for each item, then over the 36
items within each condition (with and without word definitions), then over the
two conditions. Unscored answers are missing. The human values are from
Baron-Cohen et al. (2001), Table 3, general-population controls (N = 122,
mean 26.2, SD 3.6). The difference uses a Welch t interval from the summary
statistics.

```{r}
#| label: rmet
#| code-summary: "RMET score per model and the Welch comparison"
rmet_acc <- rmet |>
  mutate(correct = if_else(is.na(choice), NA_real_,
                           as.numeric(tolower(trimws(choice)) == tolower(trimws(correct_answer))))) |>
  group_by(model_label, definitions_shown, question_id) |>
  summarise(item_acc = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(model_label, definitions_shown) |>
  summarise(acc = mean(item_acc, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(model_label) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(acc)) |>
  mutate(score36 = 36 * accuracy)

m_mod <- mean(rmet_acc$score36); s_mod <- sd(rmet_acc$score36); n_mod <- nrow(rmet_acc)
m_hum <- 26.2; s_hum <- 3.6; n_hum <- 122
se_d  <- sqrt(s_mod^2 / n_mod + s_hum^2 / n_hum)
df_w  <- se_d^4 / ((s_mod^2 / n_mod)^2 / (n_mod - 1) + (s_hum^2 / n_hum)^2 / (n_hum - 1))
d_rm  <- m_mod - m_hum
ci_rm <- d_rm + c(-1, 1) * qt(.975, df_w) * se_d

tibble(`Models` = n_mod, `Mean accuracy` = mean(rmet_acc$accuracy),
       `Mean score (of 36)` = m_mod, `SD across models` = s_mod,
       `Range` = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(rmet_acc$score36), max(rmet_acc$score36)),
       `Difference from adults` = d_rm, `Welch df` = df_w,
       `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", ci_rm[1], ci_rm[2])) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

sec <- "3.1 RMET"
loc <- "Results 3.1, l. 362–364"
check(sec, loc, "Accuracy (%)", 74, 100 * mean(rmet_acc$accuracy), digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Mean score (of 36)", 26.7, m_mod, digits = 1)
check(sec, loc, "SD across models", 3.7, s_mod, digits = 1)
check(sec, loc, "Difference from adult mean", 0.5, d_rm, digits = 1)
check(sec, loc, "95% CI lower", -1.3, ci_rm[1], digits = 1)
check(sec, loc, "95% CI upper", 2.3, ci_rm[2], digits = 1)
show_checks(sec)
```

## Section 3.3: answer change and two-run disagreement

**Claim** (lines 425–426): "21% of model–item combinations (95% CI 13% to 30%)
changed answer across five runs, and two runs disagreed in 11% of comparisons
(95% CI 7% to 17%)."

These figures use the attitude items (SDO7(s), English and Chinese SDO6, VSA)
with a numeric answer in all five runs. *Changed* means at least two different
answers across the five runs. *Two-run disagreement* is the share of the 10 pairs
of runs that gave different answers. The CIs use the pigeonhole bootstrap
(Owen, 2007), which resamples models and items independently.

The 13% to 30% interval in the manuscript comes from Table S7.1 of the
original script (`Analysis_output/stats_log.txt`: 12.99 to 30.06, from 2,000
resamples). With only 2,000 resamples the upper limit moves between about 29.4
and 30.1, depending on the random-number stream. That is enough to flip its
rounding. This notebook therefore uses 20,000 resamples, which gives stable
limits (about 12.7 to 29.9 whatever the seed). Both intervals round to the
whole percentages printed.

```{r}
#| label: change
#| code-summary: "Per-pair change and disagreement, then the pigeonhole bootstrap"
pairs_df <- att |>
  mutate(item = paste(instrument, language, question_id)) |>
  group_by(model_label, item) |>
  filter(sum(!is.na(value)) == 5L, n() == 5L) |>
  arrange(run, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(changed = as.numeric(n_distinct(value) > 1),
            disagree = mean(combn(value, 2, function(v) v[1] != v[2])))

as_matrix <- function(df, v) {
  w <- df |> select(model_label, item, all_of(v)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = item, values_from = all_of(v))
  M <- as.matrix(w[, -1]); rownames(M) <- w$model_label; M
}
set.seed(SEED); bc <- crossed_boot(as_matrix(pairs_df, "changed"))
set.seed(SEED); bd <- crossed_boot(as_matrix(pairs_df, "disagree"))

tibble(Measure = c("Changed across five runs", "Two-run disagreement"),
       `Complete pairs` = nrow(pairs_df),
       `Estimate (%)` = 100 * c(bc["estimate"], bd["estimate"]),
       `95% CI lower` = 100 * c(bc["lower"], bd["lower"]),
       `95% CI upper` = 100 * c(bc["upper"], bd["upper"])) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

sec <- "3.3 Change"
loc <- "Results 3.3, l. 425–426"
check(sec, loc, "Changed (%)", 21, 100 * bc[["estimate"]], digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Changed, 95% CI lower (%)", 13, 100 * bc[["lower"]], digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Changed, 95% CI upper (%)", 30, 100 * bc[["upper"]], digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Two-run disagreement (%)", 11, 100 * bd[["estimate"]], digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Disagreement, 95% CI lower (%)", 7, 100 * bd[["lower"]], digits = 0)
check(sec, loc, "Disagreement, 95% CI upper (%)", 17, 100 * bd[["upper"]], digits = 0)
show_checks(sec)
```

## Section 3.3: models in the generation comparison

**Claim** (lines 471–474): "The comparison included 19 models from two
developers (10 earlier, 9 later; the two open-weight GPT-OSS models belong to
neither generation and were excluded)".

Generation labels follow Supplementary Table S2: GPT-4 and Claude 4 are
earlier, GPT-5 and Claude 5 are later.

```{r}
#| label: generations
#| code-summary: "Assign generations from endpoint names"
generation_of <- function(m) {
  m <- tolower(m)
  case_when(grepl("gpt-oss", m) ~ "none (open-weight)",
            grepl("gpt-4", m) ~ "earlier", grepl("gpt-5", m) ~ "later",
            grepl("claude-[a-z]+-4|claude-[a-z]+-4-", m) ~ "earlier",
            grepl("claude-[a-z]+-5", m) ~ "later",
            TRUE ~ "other developer")
}
gen <- bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "Attitudes", model_label = unique(att$model_label)),
  tibble(set = "RMET", model_label = unique(rmet$model_label))) |>
  mutate(generation = generation_of(model_label))
gen |> count(set, generation) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  knitr::kable()
gen |> filter(set == "Attitudes") |> arrange(generation, model_label) |>
  select(generation, model_label) |> knitr::kable()

sec <- "3.3 Generations"
for (s in c("Attitudes", "RMET")) {
  g <- gen |> filter(set == s)
  check(sec, "Results 3.3, l. 471–474", paste(s, "– earlier-generation models"), 10, sum(g$generation == "earlier"), digits = 0)
  check(sec, "Results 3.3, l. 471–474", paste(s, "– later-generation models"), 9, sum(g$generation == "later"), digits = 0)
}
check(sec, "Results 3.3, l. 471–474", "Attitudes – GPT-OSS models left out", 2,
      sum(gen$set == "Attitudes" & gen$generation == "none (open-weight)"), digits = 0)
check(sec, "Results 3.3, l. 471–474", "RMET – GPT-OSS models tested", 0,
      sum(gen$set == "RMET" & gen$generation == "none (open-weight)"), digits = 0)
show_checks(sec)
```

## Human benchmarks (arithmetic only)

**Claim** (Introduction, line 109; Results 3.1, lines 370–372): the standard
deviations within the national samples of Pratto et al. (2013) "were 1.26 to
2.14 on a 1–10 scale, corresponding to roughly 0.8 to 1.4 on a 1–7 scale."

Rescaling a 1–10 scale to 1–7 multiplies standard deviations by 6/9. The 1.26
and 2.14 come from Pratto et al. (2013) and were checked against the paper.
They are not recomputed from our data.

```{r}
#| label: pratto
#| code-summary: "Rescale the Pratto et al. (2013) SDs"
sec <- "Benchmarks"
check(sec, "Results 3.1, l. 370–372", "Pratto lowest SD on 1–7 (1.26 × 6/9)", 0.8, 1.26 * 6 / 9, digits = 1)
check(sec, "Results 3.1, l. 370–372", "Pratto highest SD on 1–7 (2.14 × 6/9)", 1.4, 2.14 * 6 / 9, digits = 1)
show_checks(sec)
```

The Introduction (lines 113–115) now credits the Bizumic and Duckitt (2018)
results to the studies that reported them. The voter-group SDs (1.3 to 1.6)
come from Study 2 (UK adults). The note that every item spanned −4 to +4 comes
from Appendix B, Table B1, which is Study 1 (Australian undergraduates). This
is a source check, so there is nothing to recompute.

## Which tests are one-sided?

**Claim** (Methods, lines 322–328): "Tests were two-sided (α = .05) except the
equivalence tests and the permutation tests of shared wrong answers and of item
coherence, which were one-sided."

This is read from the code in `Analysis_script/02_statistical_analysis.R`,
not recomputed:

| Test (Table S4 row) | How the P value is computed | Sidedness |
|---|---|---|
| Two erring models choosing the same wrong word | share of permutations with P(same) ≥ observed | one-sided |
| Same wrong word, same versus different developers | share of permutations with excess ≥ observed | one-sided |
| Items with the same keying / same subscale cohere more | exact permutation, within-minus-between r ≥ observed | one-sided |
| RMET equivalence (±1.8 items) and definitions (±5 points) | two one-sided tests (TOST) | one-sided by design |
| Concentration of wrong answers; session-label test | upper tail of a non-negative statistic (like a chi-square test) | not directional |
| All t, Wilcoxon, likelihood-ratio, meta-regression and correlation tests; bootstrap drift test | two-sided | two-sided |
